subject.title: Telegram owner commands: trusted execution mode for approval-gated actions

question: Should OpenClaw add a trusted-owner approval-bypass mode for Telegram group-origin privileged actions, and should that policy live in shared approval/elevated/tool-class logic instead of a Telegram-only boolean?
rationale: The requested behavior is absent, but deciding when a chat identity may skip approval prompts changes a security boundary and config contract that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design shared trusted-owner policy
options.body: Add a disabled-by-default policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the existing approval stack.

options.title: Keep existing approval model
options.body: Decline a scoped bypass and document that operators who want no prompts must use the existing broad exec/elevated full path with permissive host approvals.

options.title: Add Telegram-only shortcut
options.body: Implement a Telegram config directly, accepting a smaller patch but higher long-term policy drift risk across channel approval clients.

recommendation.title: Design shared trusted-owner policy
recommendation.body: Add a disabled-by-default policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the existing approval stack.

likelyOwner.reason: Their prior owner-fallback change is the closest current Telegram approval identity boundary for this decision.
